summary: drafted plugin/check-plugin-manifests (11 scenarios, 1:1 with the map) as a behavioral child under plugin/, leaving the frozen plugin.feature untouched

build-to-learn spike over the real tree: 46 pointers across 11 manifests, zero false positives on the relative-path pointer rule, exactly the three known-dead pointers caught; publish-check rule clean on both publishable packages

spike found a prose-impl contradiction in the parent node: plugin/README asserted the sdd package is private with no npm publish and listed a cursor marketplace file. Neither holds — the package carries no private field and is published, and that file is absent. Load-bearing for this node because it decides whether the publish check applies here at all. Corrected in the same change; single instance, swept.

OPEN QUESTION for the owner, not resolved here: the marketplace caches an installed plugin under its manifest version, and the aced manifest stays at 0.1.0 after this fix, so an already-installed user may keep the cached copy carrying the dead key. Manifest versions are not maintained in lockstep in this repo (the sdd manifest reads 0.0.0 against a published package at 0.2.1), so the bump convention is unclear and is the owner release call rather than a guess to make inside the CR.

detail: spec gate returned blocked before grading: the declared spec-producer governance set omitted gate-validation, one of the fixed-universal bars start-mission names for loading at a gate. No enum cause covers a pre-flight declaration miss, so the off-enum value is written and flagged as an enum-growth candidate.

the parent-node prose correction overreached: it asserted the marketplace and npm routes must agree, a guarantee no scenario in the child suite checks. Softened to state what each route requires and what the node actually verifies, rather than backing the claim with a cross-route scenario that would be a different capability.

summary: deliver data fix landed, and it exposed a tree fact the engine must handle: the codex manifest is a symlink to the canonical source for two of the three plugins but a real file for the third, so the eleven manifest paths are backed by nine real files. Stripping the canonical key cleaned all three aced paths at once. Reporting stays keyed on path rather than inode, because an installer resolves a path. Checked the one real codex copy for pointer drift against its canonical source: none, it differs only in its vendor schema URL.

re-drove the spec under the full producer procedure after loading it properly. governances_loaded (12): sdd:spec-producer-governance, sdd:spec-format-governance, sdd:suite-format-governance, sdd:spec-structure-governance, sdd:lifecycle-governance, sdd:gate-validation-governance, sdd:ownership-governance, sdd:combat-log-governance, sdd:remediation-governance, sdd:oracle-spec-governance, sdd:builder-spec-governance, sdd:architect-spec-governance. The first two rounds ran the role without ever reading its own procedure, which is why the pre-flight miss happened.

detail: the pairwise-consistency bar caught a contradiction the form check passes clean: three scenarios asserted the run exits zero without scoping the tree, so a snapshot holding both a clean manifest and a dead pointer satisfied both those scenarios and the failing ones at once. Each of the three Givens now scopes the whole tree.

the Given apparatus bar was not applied on the first draft: conjunctions were not split into one condition per step, a defined shorthand stood in for the concrete fact the reader must build, and the empty-tree state was anchored on nothing present. Every Given re-authored against the build test.

summary: round 2 produced no verdict: the cold judge died of context exhaustion after exploring the spec corpus broadly. A dispatch defect on my side, not a grading result — the brief named the subject without bounding the read set against a large tree. Round 3 re-dispatched with an explicit read budget, named files, and a do-not-read list.

round 3 also produced no verdict, failing at launch on prompt length rather than mid-run. Measured cause: the shipped spec-judge agent is pinned to a model whose context is smaller than its own mandated load. Its governance floor alone runs to roughly a thousand lines before it opens a single spec file, and the one round that did return consumed more tokens than that model holds, so it only survived by compacting. Two of three dispatches died. Re-dispatched with a model override. This is a defect in the shipped agent, not in this CR, and is a follow-up candidate for handoff.

detail: builder lens failed on discrimination, not on branch reach: three rules the node states in prose could not register a miss, so a wrong subject violating them passed every scenario. The value-shape rule (a pointer is any relative path, not a hardcoded key list) had no Given naming any key at all; the publish-skip extension is a disjunction and only its private half was covered; and the sole surface element had no scenario, leaving the flag guard without a positive companion. Two continue edges and the short-circuit were likewise stated and unasserted. Six scenarios added, map and CFG realigned.

summary: substantiated the untested-disjunct finding against the live tree and it is worse than reported: every package here declares a files allowlist, so the absent-allowlist branch has no live instance either. A guard inverting that semantic would ship green through this repo and only misfire in a consumer repo. Recorded because the measurement, not the finding, is what justifies the scenario.

architect observation adopted into the record: the parent prose correction is coupled to the child rule rather than cosmetic. Correcting the sdd package from private to publishing turns the publish sub-check ON for that plugin own manifests, which the whole-tree sweep already measured clean. A later reader should not read that edit as documentation-only.

detail: impl gate returned implementation-pass false on one falsely-verified scenario: the unrecognized-flag fixture carried a dead pointer, so an engine that ignored the flag exited non-zero for the other reason and the test could not tell rejection from ignoring. Neither Then clause was bound — nothing captured stderr, and nothing distinguished checking-no-manifest. Fixture given a resolving pointer and both streams captured. Verification-only; the engine was correct as written.

the structural read found four behaviors the engine implements that no frozen scenario reaches, the heaviest being array traversal. Reproduced it: deleting array recursion left every per-scenario test green and the real tree still reporting clean, while silently dropping twelve live agent pointers. Closed with inner-layer unit tests as the pyramid base rather than by editing the frozen suite. The contract gap itself is a follow-up.

summary: chasing one surviving mutant found a defect neither judge did. The negated-allowlist-entry filter was dead code — an exclusion carries its marker in its first segment, so it can never equal a real segment and the filter changed nothing, which is why no test could bind it. Removing it exposed the real bug it hid: an allowlist entry spelled with a leading relative prefix failed to match a pointer that always carries one, so the guard would report a genuinely shipped component as unpublished. Both sides are now normalized before comparison, and the normalization is bound in both directions. Full sweep: sixteen mutants, sixteen caught, no survivors.

detail: impl gate round two found the verification bound one level below the contract subject. Every frozen When says the guard runs and every Then is a claim about what it says and what the run exits with, but the checks asserted the in-memory finding array instead of the CLI. Nine plausible mutants shipped green through that gap, including a guard that prints all-manifests-OK while exiting non-zero, one that writes its report to the wrong stream, and one that names the wrong file as unreadable. All seventeen scenarios re-bound at the CLI boundary; all nine survivors now caught.

summary: the judge correction to the allowlist diagnosis is itself wrong and is not adopted. It reconstructed the pre-fix comparison with neither side normalized; in fact the pointer side always was and only the entry side was not, which inverts its table. Reproduced both variants side by side: the plain spelling worked before the fix and the prefixed spelling was the one that failed. The fix is unaffected since both spellings now match, so this is a record correction rather than a code change. Its two genuine structural findings, plus a latent wildcard-allowlist case it spotted, were adopted.

final verification posture: thirty checks, seventeen frozen scenarios bound at the CLI boundary and thirteen inner-layer rules beneath them. Mutation sweep across twenty-five distinct wrong implementations, drawn from both my own set and the judge independent set, with no survivors. pnpm verify exits zero at 1279 tests.

detail: impl gate round three: the plugin-root branch that distinguishes a package-root manifest from a one-level-down one was unverified. Reproduced the blocker — forcing the one-level-down rule for every manifest survives the whole suite while reporting a real, correctly-shipped component as missing in this very repo. The existing package-root check used a dead pointer, which cannot tell the two rules apart. Bound with a resolving pointer, plus discovery-order determinism and a flag near-miss.

the engine named its manifest-location constant for vendors while including the directory the spec Key terms define as canonical. A careful reader took the constant as the vocabulary and concluded a scenario fixture violated its own Given. The spec is the authority and the fixture was right, but the collision was mine: renamed to a path-shape name with a comment stating that one of the three holds the canonical manifest and the other two its generated copies.

summary: the allowlist disagreement is settled in my favour: the judge re-ran all three candidate forms and withdrew its round-two finding, noting the pre-fix text is unrecoverable from git because the file is untracked. It also verified both wrong forms die against the shipped code, so the fix is confirmed in both directions regardless of which reconstruction was right.
